message.content:
Capture real screenshots of the Nxeon platform's public UI for use as blog images. This is a CAPTURE-ONLY task: do NOT deploy, do NOT run prisma, do NOT restart any service, do NOT promote anything. Just produce image files and report.

Environment: repo at /opt/nxeon. The live public marketing site is https://nxeon.cloud (already deployed, healthy). Its public marketing pages contain polished "showcase" UI components that render mocked system screens (a server dashboard, a mail inbox, a DNS manager, migration screens, metrics, game-server panels, etc.).

Steps:
1. In /opt/nxeon, install Playwright chromium locally: `npm i -D playwright` then `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` (if --with-deps fails on missing apt permissions, retry without it: `npx playwright install chromium`).
2. First DISCOVER the good public routes and the CSS selectors of the nicest showcase sections. Read the marketing pages under /opt/nxeon/app (the homepage app/page.tsx or app/(marketing), plus app/pricing, app/features if present, app/blog, and the free-tools / domain pages). Look at components/marketing/* for the showcase components (dashboard, mail inbox, DNS manager, migration, metrics) and note stable selectors (ids, data-attributes, or distinctive class names / headings) you can target.
3. Write a throwaway script /opt/nxeon/scripts/capture-screens.mjs that launches headless chromium at viewport 1440x900, deviceScaleFactor 2, navigates to each target URL on https://nxeon.cloud, waits for network idle + a short settle, and captures:
   - Full-section ELEMENT screenshots of each showcase component (element.screenshot() — these look far better than full-page shots). Use locator/elementHandle by the selectors you found.
   - A few clean page shots (pricing table, blog index, a free tool, the domain generator) — for these, screenshot a bounded region (clip) or the main content element, not the whole scrolling page.
   Save PNGs to /opt/nxeon/public/blog/screenshots/ with descriptive kebab-case names, e.g. server-dashboard.png, mail-inbox.png, dns-manager.png, migration-center.png, metrics-monitoring.png, deploy-wizard.png, pricing-plans.png, game-servers.png, domain-generator.png, free-tools.png, blog-index.png. Aim for 10–16 images.
4. Verify: every PNG exists and is > 15KB (reject blank/tiny captures). Re-target any that came out blank or full-of-header by adjusting the selector/scroll. It's fine to drop a target that won't capture cleanly — quality over count.
5. Do NOT commit. Leave the PNGs in place. Optionally leave scripts/capture-screens.mjs in place (I'll decide whether to keep it).

Report back: the exact list of successfully-captured files with their public paths (form: /blog/screenshots/NAME.png) and a one-line description of what each shows (e.g. "server-dashboard.png — VPS list with CPU/RAM gauges"). This mapping is what I'll use to attach images to blog posts, so be accurate about which file shows what.
